title: Habits
intro: Small things that keep you steady. Pick one, not ten. Start it, and if you like, keep track. No streaks, no scores.

ui.none: No habits yet. Pick one below: just one is plenty.
ui.addPlaceholder: For example: call Mum on Sundays
ui.deleteConfirm: Delete this habit and its history?

habits.title: Eat one real meal
habits.why: Heartbreak kills appetite. A real meal is the floor everything else stands on.
habits.how: Sit down, plate, no phone. It doesn't need to be fancy.

habits.title: Go outside for a walk
habits.why: Moving your body moves feelings through it, and daylight helps sleep.

habits.title: Wake up at the same time
habits.why: Sleep resets from the morning end, not the night end. A fixed wake-up time does more than an early bedtime.
habits.how: Same time every day, weekends too. Light on your face soon after.

habits.title: Phone out of the bedroom
habits.why: Scrolling in bed feels like rest, but it keeps your brain switched on, and her profile is one tap away.
habits.how: Charge it in another room. Use a cheap alarm clock.

habits.title: Feel one feeling, fully
habits.why: Feelings you push away stick around; feelings you let in move through.
habits.how: Once a day, sit for two minutes. Ask: what am I feeling? Where in my body? Let it be there without fixing it.

habits.title: Five minutes of quiet
habits.why: A few minutes of sitting still trains you to notice thoughts without obeying them.
habits.how: Sit, breathe, watch a candle or your breath. When your mind wanders, come back. That's the whole practice.

habits.title: Ask someone a real question
habits.why: Curiosity about other people is the quickest way out of your own head, and the start of every friendship.
habits.how: Not "how are you". Something you actually want to know.

habits.title: Reach out to one person
habits.why: Friendships fade when nobody goes first. Be the one who goes first.
habits.how: A message, a voice note, a call. "Saw this and thought of you" counts.

habits.title: Go back to the same place
habits.why: Friendship is mostly showing up to the same place at the same time until you're a regular.
habits.how: The same café, club, game night or class, each week.

habits.title: Cook for someone
habits.why: Giving is one of the fastest ways back to feeling useful, and food brings people to a table.
habits.how: A neighbour, a friend, a pot of soup in the courtyard.

habits.title: Say one true feeling out loud
habits.why: Many men only let anger out. Naming the other feelings makes them smaller, and makes you easier to be close to.
habits.how: To a friend, your sister, a therapist, or the mirror: "I'm sad", "I'm scared", "I miss her".
